overview: F. W. Lee sought recovery on eleven 1931 Taiwan Electric bonds; Senator Tydings relayed his inquiry to Acheson, believing the company's assets were federally held. State explained the company operated in Chinese-administered Taiwan, that Congress hadn't resolved paying Japanese-guaranteed securities from vested assets, and directed Lee to the Bondholders Council.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Senator Tydings concerning F. W. Lee’s Taiwan Electric Company bonds
subfiles.from: Ernest A. Gross, Assistant Secretary of State, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Millard E. Tydings, United States Senate
subfiles.about: The Department explains the uncertain legal and diplomatic status of F. W. Lee’s Japanese-guaranteed Taiwan Electric Company bonds and recommends that he work through the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council.
subfiles.summary: State tells Tydings Lee's bonds were part of a 1931 Morgan-underwritten, Japan-guaranteed issue; payment from vested Japanese assets awaits Congress, the company's property lies in Chinese-administered Taiwan, and Lee is directed to the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, since foreign securities remain private investments.

subfiles.title: Senator Tydings’s inquiry to Secretary Acheson about F. W. Lee’s bond claim
subfiles.from: Millard E. Tydings, chairman, Senate Committee on Armed Services
subfiles.about: Senator Tydings asks the State Department for information about a constituent’s claim involving eleven Taiwan Electric Company bonds.
subfiles.summary: Tydings relays Lee's claim on eleven 1935-purchased Taiwan Electric bonds, paid until December 1942, with Lee believing the company's property was federally held, asking Acheson for information.

interest: Shows how prewar Japanese-guaranteed Taiwan bonds became entangled with postwar claims policy and vested-asset questions.
